front_blocks.md: Define **tourism**.

back_blocks.md: **Tourism** is time spent away from the **home environment** for **leisure, business or professional** reasons. It is one aspect of **globalisation**.

cards.front_md: Define **tourism**.
cards.back_md: **Tourism** is time spent away from the **home environment** for **leisure, business or professional** reasons. It is one aspect of **globalisation**.

front_blocks.md: How have **low-cost airlines** helped tourism grow?

back_blocks.md: Airlines such as **easyJet** and **Ryanair** have led to **cheaper and faster air travel**, making international travel more accessible.

cards.front_md: How have **low-cost airlines** helped tourism grow?
cards.back_md: Airlines such as **easyJet** and **Ryanair** have led to **cheaper and faster air travel**, making international travel more accessible.

front_blocks.md: Give **two economic factors** behind the growth of tourism.

back_blocks.md: Increased **disposable incomes** (often both partners working, especially in emerging economies); better **pay and leave benefits** (paid annual leave, sub-40-hour weeks); and globalisation **expanding middle-class** populations.

cards.front_md: Give **two economic factors** behind the growth of tourism.
cards.back_md: Increased **disposable incomes** (often both partners working, especially in emerging economies); better **pay and leave benefits** (paid annual leave, sub-40-hour weeks); and globalisation **expanding middle-class** populations.

front_blocks.md: How have **technological developments** boosted tourism?

back_blocks.md: **Online booking platforms** such as **Booking.com** and **Airbnb**, **instant access to information** via smartphones, and the **social media effect** of tourists sharing experiences.

cards.front_md: How have **technological developments** boosted tourism?

front_blocks.md: In **2024**, what proportion of global GDP did the tourism industry account for?

back_blocks.md: **10%** of global GDP, contributing **\$10.9 trillion** to the global economy and supporting **357 million jobs** worldwide.

front_blocks.md: Who proposed the **Butler model**, and in what year?

back_blocks.md: **Richard W. Butler** proposed it in **1980**.

cards.front_md: Who proposed the **Butler model**, and in what year?
cards.back_md: **Richard W. Butler** proposed it in **1980**.

front_blocks.md: Name the **first three stages** of the Butler model, in order.

back_blocks.md: **1. Exploration** (small numbers of adventurous tourists), **2. Involvement** (locals offer basic services), **3. Development** (larger companies invest and tourist numbers rise rapidly).

cards.front_md: Name the **first three stages** of the Butler model, in order.
cards.back_md: **1. Exploration** (small numbers of adventurous tourists), **2. Involvement** (locals offer basic services), **3. Development** (larger companies invest and tourist numbers rise rapidly).

front_blocks.md: What happens during the **stagnation** stage of the Butler model?

back_blocks.md: Visitor numbers **peak**, the **environment and local culture may suffer**, and the resort **loses appeal** due to overcrowding and loss of authenticity.

cards.front_md: What happens during the **stagnation** stage of the Butler model?
cards.back_md: Visitor numbers **peak**, the **environment and local culture may suffer**, and the resort **loses appeal** due to overcrowding and loss of authenticity.

front_blocks.md: What are the **three possible outcomes** after stagnation in the Butler model?

back_blocks.md: **Rejuvenation** (reinventing itself, e.g. eco-tourism/heritage tourism), **continued stagnation** (minimum investment, fails to adapt), or **decline** (tourists leave, businesses close, area deteriorates).

cards.front_md: What are the **three possible outcomes** after stagnation in the Butler model?
cards.back_md: **Rejuvenation** (reinventing itself, e.g. eco-tourism/heritage tourism), **continued stagnation** (minimum investment, fails to adapt), or **decline** (tourists leave, businesses close, area deteriorates).

front_blocks.md: Give **two limitations** of the Butler model.

back_blocks.md: It is **simple** — real development rarely follows clear stages; it ignores **global shocks** like pandemics and terrorism; and **external factors** such as climate change and economic crises are poorly represented.

cards.front_md: Give **two limitations** of the Butler model.
cards.back_md: It is **simple** — real development rarely follows clear stages; it ignores **global shocks** like pandemics and terrorism; and **external factors** such as climate change and economic crises are poorly represented.

front_blocks.md: During the **______** stage of the Butler model, tourism becomes the dominant economic activity and the destination gains a strong reputation, but negative impacts such as pollution and congestion begin to emerge.

back_blocks.md: During the **consolidation** stage of the Butler model, tourism becomes the dominant economic activity and the destination gains a strong reputation, but negative impacts such as pollution and congestion begin to emerge.

cards.front_md: During the **______** stage of the Butler model, tourism becomes the dominant economic activity and the destination gains a strong reputation, but negative impacts such as pollution and congestion begin to emerge.
cards.back_md: During the **consolidation** stage of the Butler model, tourism becomes the dominant economic activity and the destination gains a strong reputation, but negative impacts such as pollution and congestion begin to emerge.

The Butler model can be applied to a wide range of different destinations.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
A strength of the Butler model is that it is **flexible** and can be applied to a wide range of destinations, offering a clear visual representation of how tourism evolves.

front_blocks.md: What does the **Butler model** describe?

back_blocks.md: The **life cycle of tourist resorts** — how tourism changes over time and how destinations can handle their growth.

front_blocks.md: Define the **multiplier effect** in tourism.

back_blocks.md: When tourists **spend money**, it **circulates in the local economy** and helps suppliers and service providers, generating further income and jobs.

cards.front_md: Define the **multiplier effect** in tourism.
cards.back_md: When tourists **spend money**, it **circulates in the local economy** and helps suppliers and service providers, generating further income and jobs.

front_blocks.md: How do **foreign exchange earnings** from tourism benefit a country?

back_blocks.md: International tourists spend on travel, accommodation and food, which helps **stabilise the local currency**, finance **imports**, and invest in building **new infrastructure**.

cards.front_md: How do **foreign exchange earnings** from tourism benefit a country?
cards.back_md: International tourists spend on travel, accommodation and food, which helps **stabilise the local currency**, finance **imports**, and invest in building **new infrastructure**.

front_blocks.md: Give **two social benefits** of tourism.

back_blocks.md: **Cultural exchange** (building understanding between cultures), **preservation of culture** (traditional crafts, festivals, heritage), improved **services** (healthcare, education), and greater **social mobility**.

cards.front_md: Give **two social benefits** of tourism.
cards.back_md: **Cultural exchange** (building understanding between cultures), **preservation of culture** (traditional crafts, festivals, heritage), improved **services** (healthcare, education), and greater **social mobility**.

front_blocks.md: How can tourism benefit the **environment**?

back_blocks.md: Through **conservation funding** (entrance fees, ecotourism), **awareness raising**, **restoration projects**, and **wildlife protection** — human presence deters poaching and illegal activity in protected areas.

cards.front_md: How can tourism benefit the **environment**?
cards.back_md: Through **conservation funding** (entrance fees, ecotourism), **awareness raising**, **restoration projects**, and **wildlife protection** — human presence deters poaching and illegal activity in protected areas.

front_blocks.md: Name two countries where tourism significantly boosts **GDP**.

back_blocks.md: The **Maldives** and **Thailand**.

cards.front_md: Name two countries where tourism significantly boosts **GDP**.
cards.back_md: The **Maldives** and **Thailand**.

front_blocks.md: Define **economic leakage** in tourism.

back_blocks.md: Where **profits flow to foreign-owned companies** instead of helping the **local economy**.

cards.front_md: Define **economic leakage** in tourism.
cards.back_md: Where **profits flow to foreign-owned companies** instead of helping the **local economy**.

front_blocks.md: Define **acculturation** as a problem of tourism.

back_blocks.md: Where **culture becomes a product** — traditions change or are performed to satisfy tourists, causing a **loss of local language and traditional values**.

cards.front_md: Define **acculturation** as a problem of tourism.
cards.back_md: Where **culture becomes a product** — traditions change or are performed to satisfy tourists, causing a **loss of local language and traditional values**.

front_blocks.md: Give **two economic problems** caused by tourism.

back_blocks.md: **Seasonal jobs** causing insecurity and fluctuating income; **low wages** with few advancement chances; **economic leakages**; and **over-reliance**, leaving economies vulnerable to shocks like pandemics.

cards.front_md: Give **two economic problems** caused by tourism.
cards.back_md: **Seasonal jobs** causing insecurity and fluctuating income; **low wages** with few advancement chances; **economic leakages**; and **over-reliance**, leaving economies vulnerable to shocks like pandemics.

front_blocks.md: How can tourism cause **social tensions** among local residents?

back_blocks.md: Locals may feel **resentment** if benefits are not shared fairly — e.g. **loss of access** to local sites like beaches and forests — and **inflation** can raise land, housing and goods prices.

cards.front_md: How can tourism cause **social tensions** among local residents?
cards.back_md: Locals may feel **resentment** if benefits are not shared fairly — e.g. **loss of access** to local sites like beaches and forests — and **inflation** can raise land, housing and goods prices.

front_blocks.md: Give **two environmental problems** caused by tourism.

back_blocks.md: **Environmental degradation** (footpath erosion, coral reef damage, deforestation), **pollution** (waste, sewage, air), **resource pressure** (water/energy in fragile areas), and a high **carbon footprint** from air travel.

cards.front_md: Give **two environmental problems** caused by tourism.
cards.back_md: **Environmental degradation** (footpath erosion, coral reef damage, deforestation), **pollution** (waste, sewage, air), **resource pressure** (water/energy in fragile areas), and a high **carbon footprint** from air travel.

Tourism only ever damages culture and never helps to preserve it.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Tourism can **preserve culture** by encouraging the preservation of **traditional crafts, festivals and heritage sites**, although acculturation can also damage local traditions.

front_blocks.md: Define **sustainable tourism**.

back_blocks.md: Tourism that takes full account of its current and future **economic, social and environmental** impacts, addressing the needs of **visitors, the industry, the environment and host communities** (WTO definition).

cards.front_md: Define **sustainable tourism**.
cards.back_md: Tourism that takes full account of its current and future **economic, social and environmental** impacts, addressing the needs of **visitors, the industry, the environment and host communities** (WTO definition).

front_blocks.md: What are the **three scales** at which strategies manage tourism sustainably?

back_blocks.md: **International** (global organisations/cooperation), **national** (governments/regional authorities), and **individual/local** (communities, businesses and tourists).

cards.front_md: What are the **three scales** at which strategies manage tourism sustainably?
cards.back_md: **International** (global organisations/cooperation), **national** (governments/regional authorities), and **individual/local** (communities, businesses and tourists).

front_blocks.md: Give **two international strategies** for sustainable tourism.

back_blocks.md: **UNESCO World Heritage Site** designation (funding and guidance), **international guidelines** like the WTO Global Code of Ethics, and **global eco-certification schemes** such as Green Globe and EarthCheck.

cards.front_md: Give **two international strategies** for sustainable tourism.
cards.back_md: **UNESCO World Heritage Site** designation (funding and guidance), **international guidelines** like the WTO Global Code of Ethics, and **global eco-certification schemes** such as Green Globe and EarthCheck.

front_blocks.md: What is **Bhutan's** tourism policy an example of?

back_blocks.md: A national **visitor quota** strategy — its **'High Value, Low Impact'** policy limits tourist numbers to avoid overcrowding.

cards.front_md: What is **Bhutan's** tourism policy an example of?
cards.back_md: A national **visitor quota** strategy — its **'High Value, Low Impact'** policy limits tourist numbers to avoid overcrowding.

front_blocks.md: How does **Venice** plan to use tourism taxation sustainably?

back_blocks.md: Venice plans to charge an **entrance fee to day-trippers**, using tourist taxes to fund local conservation and infrastructure.

cards.front_md: How does **Venice** plan to use tourism taxation sustainably?
cards.back_md: Venice plans to charge an **entrance fee to day-trippers**, using tourist taxes to fund local conservation and infrastructure.

front_blocks.md: Define **community-based tourism**.

back_blocks.md: Where **locals run small-scale enterprises**, keeping income within the community — for example, **homestay schemes in Nepal**.

cards.front_md: Define **community-based tourism**.
cards.back_md: Where **locals run small-scale enterprises**, keeping income within the community — for example, **homestay schemes in Nepal**.

front_blocks.md: Give **two individual/local strategies** for sustainable tourism.

back_blocks.md: **Eco-friendly accommodation** (solar power, rainwater harvesting), **community-based tourism**, **tourist education** (codes of conduct, carbon offsetting, flying less), and promoting **off-season tourism**.

cards.front_md: Give **two individual/local strategies** for sustainable tourism.
cards.back_md: **Eco-friendly accommodation** (solar power, rainwater harvesting), **community-based tourism**, **tourist education** (codes of conduct, carbon offsetting, flying less), and promoting **off-season tourism**.

front_blocks.md: Give **two limitations** of **international** sustainable tourism strategies.

back_blocks.md: They are **voluntary** so enforcement is weak, adoption is **small-scale** (many operators don't participate), and **certification costs** are high for small businesses.

cards.front_md: Give **two limitations** of **international** sustainable tourism strategies.
cards.back_md: They are **voluntary** so enforcement is weak, adoption is **small-scale** (many operators don't participate), and **certification costs** are high for small businesses.

front_blocks.md: What are the **strengths** of **national** sustainable tourism strategies?

back_blocks.md: They are **legally enforceable**, have **large-scale impact** (governments coordinate wide campaigns), and **generate funding** for local communities and conservation.

cards.front_md: What are the **strengths** of **national** sustainable tourism strategies?
cards.back_md: They are **legally enforceable**, have **large-scale impact** (governments coordinate wide campaigns), and **generate funding** for local communities and conservation.

front_blocks.md: Give one **strength** of individual/local strategies.

back_blocks.md: Empowers **local people** and can preserve **cultural identity**.

cards.front_md: Give one **strength** of individual/local strategies.
cards.back_md: Empowers **local people** and can preserve **cultural identity**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
National sustainable tourism strategies are guaranteed to last because political will never changes.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
**Political will can fluctuate** — new governments may reverse policies — and enforcement in remote areas is challenging, with resistance from businesses reliant on mass tourism.
